by a valid return. Verification finishes quickly, but bpf_opt_remove_nops()
then spends a long time removing each jump separately. Since this
post-verification work neither checks for signals nor reschedules, a pending
SIGKILL cannot terminate the task until the rewrite finishes.

Make bpf_patch_insn_data() and verifier_remove_insns() common cancellation
and rescheduling points. These helpers run from BPF_PROG_LOAD process
context, and bpf_patch_insn_data() can already sleep while reallocating
auxiliary data.

Report interrupted constant blinding as -EINTR and propagate it through
both JIT paths, including kernels that permit interpreter fallback.
Other blinding failures retain the existing fallback behavior.

This does not reduce the quadratic cost of the rewrite passes, but it makes
the work preemptible and allows a killed loader to be torn down promptly.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: smb: client: drain and invalidate before server-side copy/clone
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: drain and invalidate before server-side copy/clone

cifs_file_copychunk_range() and the clone (FICLONE) path of
cifs_remap_file_range() do not serialise the destination page cache
against the server-side copy the way the other server-side range
operations (smb3_zero_range(), smb3_punch_hole(), smb3_collapse_range()
and smb3_insert_range()) do.

cifs_file_copychunk_range() invalidates the destination range with
filemap_invalidate_inode(), which takes and drops the mapping's
invalidate_lock internally, so the lock is no longer held when the
copychunk ioctl is issued.  It also never drains in-flight netfs I/O on
the target.  The clone path never takes the invalidate_lock at all (only
i_rwsem), uses a bare truncate_inode_pages_range() and likewise does not
drain outstanding I/O.

As a result an asynchronous destination writeback can complete after the
server-side copy/clone has run and reinstate stale data over the region
just written by the server, corrupting the file.  This is the same class
of corruption as commit d7d2adcd022b ("smb/client: flush dirty data
before punching a hole") and has been seen randomly in generic/363
against Windows Server.

Fix both paths to follow the established ordering: hold the target
mapping's invalidate_lock across the flush and invalidation of the
destination and the server ioctl, and call netfs_wait_for_outstanding_io()
on the target to drain in-flight writes before the ioctl is issued.  Only
the target inode's invalidate_lock is required, as the source is merely
flushed and not invalidated; i_rwsem (already held via
lock_two_nondirectories()) is acquired before the invalidate_lock,
matching the VFS lock ordering.  Since filemap_invalidate_inode() takes
that same lock internally, replace it with its own unmap/flush/invalidate
steps instead of calling it, and return early on a zero-length copy to
avoid a range underflow.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: smb: client: flush dirty data before zeroing a range
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: flush dirty data before zeroing a range

smb3_zero_range() emulates FALLOC_FL_ZERO_RANGE by invalidating the
page cache over the target range with truncate_pagecache_range() and
then issuing FSCTL_SET_ZERO_DATA to the server.

Dirty data was only flushed conditionally, when the range reached or
extended EOF.  For a purely interior zero range that does not reach
EOF, no flush happened, so a dirty folio overlapping the range could
be written back to the server after the FSCTL and refill the range
that was just zeroed with stale data.

Fix this by unconditionally flushing and waiting for dirty data in the
range before invalidating the page cache and issuing
FSCTL_SET_ZERO_DATA, exactly as was done for smb3_punch_hole() in
commit d7d2adcd022b ("smb/client: flush dirty data before punching a
hole"); the two paths are structurally identical here.

This is observed as generic/363 randomly reading stale data where a
zeroed range is expected against Windows Server.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: smb: client: flush and commit data before querying allocated ranges
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: flush and commit data before querying allocated ranges

The mode 0 / FALLOC_FL_KEEP_SIZE fallocate emulation for small interior
ranges in smb3_simple_fallocate_range() issues
FSCTL_QUERY_ALLOCATED_RANGES and zero-fills any sub-range the server
reports as an unallocated hole, to force block allocation without
changing file contents.

This is unsafe against Windows servers.  Per the Win32 documentation,
FSCTL_QUERY_ALLOCATED_RANGES only reports ranges that *may* contain
nonzero data and is explicitly not coherent with recently written data:

  "a call to FSCTL_QUERY_ALLOCATED_RANGES [after writing to a network
   file] would not necessarily return a correct list of allocated
   regions.  To ensure coherency [...] flush the data to the file"

fsx (generic/363) reproduces the resulting corruption against Windows
Server 2022: a range is written, an uncached read returns the data, yet
the next FSCTL_QUERY_ALLOCATED_RANGES on that range reports it as a whole
hole, so the emulation overwrites live data with zeroes.  A network trace
confirmed the WRITE, the READ returning data and the query returning an
empty range list within microseconds.  Samba does not exhibit this; its
query is coherent with the written data.

Write back the dirty pages, drain any outstanding I/O and issue an SMB2
FLUSH to force the server to commit the data before querying the
allocated ranges, so the query reflects the data actually present.

With this, generic/363 passes against both Windows Server 2022 and Samba
over 100000 fsx operations.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: smb: client: discard post-EOF pagecache when extending a file via clone range
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: discard post-EOF pagecache when extending a file via clone range

cifs_remap_file_range() discarded the pagecache only for the folios
overlapping the destination region, so when a clone extends the file the
folio straddling the old EOF - which may hold data dirtied past EOF
through an mmap - was never dropped and became visible as file content
once the file was extended.

Start the discard at the smaller of fstart and the old EOF.  i_size is
still old here, so nothing past the old EOF is flushed to the server.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: seg6: ensure packet data is writable before modifying SRH and IPv6 DA
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

seg6: ensure packet data is writable before modifying SRH and IPv6 DA

advance_nextseg() modifies the SRH Segments Left field and the IPv6
destination address without ensuring the packet data is writable.
seg6_next_csid_advance_arg() has the same problem when it advances the
NEXT-C-SID argument in the destination address.

The skb may be cloned, for example by an AF_PACKET socket receiving on
the ingress device. advance_nextseg() and seg6_next_csid_advance_arg()
then write into the packet data shared with the clone. A read from that
socket can return the modified packet instead of the received one. The
simplified path below shows this for advance_nextseg():

__netif_receive_skb_one_core
  __netif_receive_skb_core
    deliver_skb               [orig: users=2, cloned=0]
      packet_rcv
        skb_clone             clone queued to the AF_PACKET socket
        consume_skb(orig)     [orig: users=1, cloned=1]
  ipv6_rcv
    ip6_rcv_core              skb_share_check: no-op [orig: users=1]
    [...]
      input_action_end_core
        advance_nextseg       writes into the data shared with the clone

Call skb_ensure_writable() in advance_nextseg() and in
seg6_next_csid_advance_arg() before they modify the packet data.
skb_ensure_writable() may reallocate skb->head, which invalidates the
pointers into the packet data taken before the call.
advance_nextseg() now returns a valid SRH pointer, or NULL if
skb_ensure_writable() fails.
seg6_next_csid_advance_arg() takes the pointer to the destination
address from the skb after skb_ensure_writable().
On failure, the callers drop the packet with SKB_DROP_REASON_NOMEM.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: wifi: iwlwifi: mld: don't WARN on WoWLAN suspend w/o netdetect
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

wifi: iwlwifi: mld: don't WARN on WoWLAN suspend w/o netdetect

Clearly, from a user perspective, it must be valid to configure
WoWLAN and then suspend while not connected to a network. Since
mac80211 doesn't distinguish these cases and simply calls the
driver to suspend whenever WoWLAN is configured, the driver has
to cleanly handle the case where it's called for WoWLAN, it's
not connected but there's also no netdetect configured.

Remove the WARN_ON() and keep returning 1 to disconnect and
then suspend.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: macsec: initialize SecY before registering the netdevice
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

macsec: initialize SecY before registering the netdevice

Creating a MACsec device with MAC offload over an LRO-capable lower
device triggers a warning in rtmsg_ifinfo_build_skb() when IPv4
forwarding is enabled by default.

register_netdevice() invokes inetdev_init(), which disables LRO and emits
a NETDEV_FEAT_CHANGE notification. This reaches macsec_fill_info() before
macsec_add_dev() initializes the SecY. key_len is still zero, so
macsec_fill_info() returns -EMSGSIZE and trips the WARN_ON in
rtmsg_ifinfo_build_skb(), even though the skb has enough space.

Even without the warning, notifications during registration can report
uninitialized SecY attributes, including the SCI. This ordering has existed
since the driver was introduced.

Initialize the SecY and apply the new-link attributes before registration.
Move MAC address inheritance into macsec_newlink() so the SCI can also be
initialized before registration-time notifications report it. Move the
per-CPU statistics and metadata destination allocation into ndo_init(),
and release partial allocations on failure.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: riscv: ptrace: Zero-initialize regset buffers before copyin
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

riscv: ptrace: Zero-initialize regset buffers before copyin

user_regset_copyin() only copies `count` bytes, so a PTRACE_SETREGSET
request with a short iov_len leaves the rest of the stack buffer
uninitialized. In riscv_vr_set() that garbage is validated and copied
into the target's vstate, and in riscv_cfi_set() it can be stored as
the target's shadow stack pointer. Zero both buffers, as the get path
already does.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: bonding: fix the program leak when XDP is replaced
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

bonding: fix the program leak when XDP is replaced

We need to release the reference on the old BPF prog, whether
we are going to no-prog, or replacing the prog with another.

Spotted by AI while running tests for the propagation series
(leaked programs were accumulating). Selftest will come in
the net-next series to avoid conflicts.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: fs: don't silently unmount busy mounts
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

fs: don't silently unmount busy mounts

The propagate_mount_busy() helper exists to decide whether a synchronous
can suceed. It does that by looking at the copies of the victims in the
mounts its parent propagates to. One of those functions from propagation
hell.

It skips a copy that has child mounts except for the case of a single
child mount covering the copy's root. That algorithm used to be exact.
It isn't anymore.

Originally only childless copies were unmounted during propagation.
And 1064f874abc0 ("mnt: Tuck mounts under others instead of creating
shadow/side mounts.") ended up adding covered mounts to both sides in
one go.

Along came 99b19d16471e ("mnt: In propgate_umount handle visiting mounts
in any order") and that started to unmount more than before:

[1]: A copy of a mount is unmounted when each of its children is either
     its overmount or a copy of the victim itself. In the former case
     the overmount gets reparented. In the latter case the copy of the
     victim will end up being unmounted.

So propagate_umount() ended up being rewritten without adjusting
propagate_mount_busy(). And currently propagate_mount_busy() doesn't
look at copies of the victim that have two or more children nor a single
child that is not the overmount.

So any such copy in [1] is not checked for
references. The result is that a synchronous unmount succeeds, pulling
out a mount that is still in use.

A container can run into this with its own mounts. The host shares a
tree with the container and the host has a mount in that tree:

  mount -t tmpfs none /mnt
  mount --make-shared /mnt
  mount -t tmpfs none /mnt/a

The container's /mnt is a slave copy of the host mount. The container
now takes a detached copy of the tree and mounts that copy beneath its
propagated copy of /mnt/a and keeps the file descriptor to the tree
open:

  unshare -m --propagation unchanged
  mount --make-rslave /
  fd = open_tree(AT_FDCWD, "/mnt", OPEN_TREE_CLONE | AT_RECURSIVE)
  move_mount(fd, "", AT_FDCWD, "/mnt/a", MOVE_MOUNT_BENEATH)

  grep /mnt /proc/self/mountinfo
  775 355 ... /mnt ...     master:646
  777 775 ... /mnt/a ...   master:646
  776 777 ... /mnt/a ...   master:647
  778 777 ... /mnt/a/a ... master:647

The now attached tree (777) is now mounted beneath the container's copy
of /mnt/a. That's also where the host mount sits (as seen from the host
mount namespace). So the propagated copy (776) of the host's mount is on
top of its root and the copy of that (778) is inside it. Now the host
runs:

  umount /mnt/a

and it succeeds. The moved tree tree and the copy inside of it are gone
from the container. Now only the propagated copy is left and it got
reparented to where it was before:

  grep /mnt /proc/self/mountinfo
  775 355 ... /mnt ... master:646
  776 775 ... /mnt/a ...

But the file descriptor still refers to the moved tree. So a synchronous
umount detached a mount that is still in use.

Teach propagate_mount_busy() the same checks that propagate_umount()
does. It now checks for a single victim mount without children
for which it can assume that MNT_LOCKED is cleared on every copy like
propagate_umount() does. The copies form chains. IOW, when a copy itself
receives propagation from the victim's parent then the mount at the same
mountpoint inside that copy is a copy as well. Whether a mount receives
propagation from the victim's can simply be checked by walking its
masters. Walk each chain once from its top so we are sure that nested
copies stay linear. Check every reference once of every copy that gets
unmounted.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: net: team: free skb when broadcast has no txable port
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net: team: free skb when broadcast has no txable port

bc_transmit() sends the original skb through the last txable port.
When no port is txable, it returns false without consuming the skb, but
team_xmit() still returns NETDEV_TX_OK. AF_PACKET sends then retain the
skb and its socket write-memory charge.

A TX-enabled, link-down port keeps the broadcast transmit op installed.
Carrier can stay up through a second link-up, TX-disabled port or be
forced on by userspace. Free the original skb on the no-port path while
leaving the existing drop accounting intact.

Discovered by Sashiko during review of previous commit.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: ipc: drop the mqueue mount with kern_unmount() on setup failure
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ipc: drop the mqueue mount with kern_unmount() on setup failure

mq_init_ns() creates the mqueue mount with fc_mount_longterm(), so its
->mnt_ns is MNT_NS_INTERNAL. When setting up the mqueue or ipc sysctls
or msg_init_ns() fails afterwards, create_ipc_ns() drops it with a plain
mntput(). With ->mnt_ns set that takes the fast path of
mntput_no_expire(). The count drops to zero and nothing ever kills the
mount, so the mount and the mqueue superblock are leaked.

Commit dc55e35f9e81 ("ipc: Store mqueue sysctls in the ipc namespace")
added the first failure path after mq_init_ns() and never dropped the
mount. Commit 7229d74e5e8c ("ipc: create_ipc_ns: drop mqueue mount on
sysctl setup failure") tried to fix that with a mntput() but that
doesn't help for a long-term mount.

Use kern_unmount(). free_ipc() open-codes the same thing for a namespace
that made it.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: information disclosure via uninitialized stack memory in KVM SynIC message delivery
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: x86: Zero reserved synic flags when delivering message to avoid stack leak

Ensure all reserved flags are zeroed when setting the msg_pending flag as
part of SynIC message delivery, as setting only msg_pending can leak seven
bits of kernel stack data to the guest.  E.g. gcc typically uses a
bitwise-OR to set the msg_pending flag, without initializing the on-stack
variable.

Precisely zero the flags, e.g. as opposed to zeroing the entire structure,
to make it somewhat more obvious that the flags *need* to be zeroed.  E.g.
it would be quite easy to misread the initial read of guest memory and
think that zeroing the entire structure is completely superfluous.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: afs: Fix afs to abort the rxrpc call on send error
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

afs: Fix afs to abort the rxrpc call on send error

Fix afs_send_empty_reply() and afs_send_simple_reply() to always try to
abort the rxrpc call rather than just aborting on -ENOMEM and otherwise
abandoning it.  If the call is already complete due to network failure or a
received abort, this will do nothing.

Also make afs_make_call() always abort on send error; again, it does
nothing if the rxrpc call is already dead.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of service via unhandled partial sends in rxrpc_kernel_send_data()
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

rxrpc: Fix lack of short-send handling in rxrpc_kernel_send_data()

Fix rxrpc_kernel_send_data() to loop around if it detects a short send.
David Laight suggested doing it here rather than wrapping all the calls in
loops.  Further, remove the len argument and use the iterator count instead
and return 0 on success, not the amount copied.

Note this is also a prerequisite for changing the way rxrpc_send_data()
works to return a short send rather than an error if some data was
buffered.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of Service via improper caching of empty group replies in SUNRPC
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

sunrpc: treat empty auth.unix.gid replies as negative entries

When rpc.mountd cannot resolve a uid (getpwuid() or getgrouplist()
failure, e.g. while winbind or sssd is briefly unreachable), it
answers the auth.unix.gid upcall with zero groups. unix_gid_parse()
installs that as a valid positive entry, and svcauth_unix_set_client()
then replaces the credential's group list with the empty one on
every request, RPCSEC_GSS included via svcauth_gss_set_client().
One failed lookup strips that uid of all supplementary groups on
every export for up to mountd's configured TTL (30 minutes by
default), long after the NSS backend has recovered.

mountd cannot send an empty list for a successful lookup, since
getgrouplist(3) always includes at least the user's primary group,
so a zero-group reply can only mean the lookup failed. Record it as
a negative entry: unix_gid_find() then returns -ENOENT and
svcauth_unix_set_client() keeps the groups the RPC credential
already carries. This is the fallback that
commit 3fc605a2aa38 ("[PATCH] knfsd: allow the server to provide a
gid list when using AUTH_UNIX authentication") promised when no
answer is available, and the same state try_to_negate_entry()
already creates when no listener holds the channel open.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of Service via unvalidated transport name in NFSD listener configuration
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

NFSD: validate transport name in listener_set before serv creation

nfsd_nl_listener_set_doit() holds nfsd_mutex for the whole listener
teardown and rebuild. The code checks NFSD_A_SOCK_TRANSPORT_NAME for
presence only, and not for content. An arbitrary name therefore reaches
svc_xprt_create_from_sa(). There, a name that matches no registered class
calls request_module("svc%s", name). That call is a TASK_KILLABLE usermode
helper upcall, and it runs under nfsd_mutex.

Check the name against the classes that NFSD can create: tcp, udp and
rdma. The check goes in nfsd_nl_validate_listeners(), which runs before
the code takes nfsd_mutex. The rejection names the offending attribute
through extack, since -EPROTONOSUPPORT on its own does not say which
entry carried the bad name.

This narrows the upcall. It does not remove it. NFSD accepts "rdma"
without a condition, so on a kernel that does not build svcrdma the name
still reaches request_module("svcrdma") under nfsd_mutex. That is
necessary for the modular case, where the autoload is legitimate.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: nfsd: Denial of Service via cache entry leak in idtoname_parse()
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

nfsd: Fix id-to-name cache entry leak in idtoname_parse()

idtoname_lookup() returns the id-to-name cache entry with a new
reference. The name is parsed between the lookup and the update call,
and when the parsed name is malformed (negative length or longer than
IDMAP_NAMESZ), idtoname_parse() jumps to the error label without
dropping the reference returned by idtoname_lookup(), leaking the cache
entry.

Release the reference with cache_put() before taking the error exit.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Data corruption via missing lock validation in NFS flexfiles client
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

NFSv4/flexfiles: fail I/O to the data server once a lock is lost

When a client loses a byte-range lock, because its lease expired and it
may not recover the lock (nfs.recover_lost_locks=0) or because reclaim
failed, it marks the lock state NFS_LOCK_LOST and fails further I/O by
that lock owner.  Otherwise an application that believes it holds a
lock over a range is never told that the lock is gone, and can
overwrite data that another client has since written under its own
lock on that range.

The NFSv4 READ/WRITE and file layout I/O paths apply this in
rpc_call_prepare, where nfs4_set_rw_stateid() returns -EIO for a lost
lock.  The flexfiles data server I/O path does not: the NFSv3 data
server path never checked, and the check on the NFSv4 path was removed
when the data server stateid began to be taken from the layout.

Fail read and write RPCs to the data server in rpc_call_prepare when the
lock is lost.  The data server path has no use for the stateid that
nfs4_set_rw_stateid() selects, and selecting it looks up a delegation
or open stateid on every I/O.
Instead add nfs4_lock_context_lost(), which only tests NFS_LOCK_LOST,
and check it alongside the open state.  Its lookup,
__nfs4_lookup_lock_state(), is split out of __nfs4_find_lock_state()
and takes no reference: a lock state is only unlinked from
state->lock_states under state->state_lock, so one found while holding
that lock cannot be freed before it is released.  Use it in
nfs4_copy_lock_stateid() as well, which only reads the lock state under
that lock.  That drops a reference get and put from stateid selection
for all NFSv4 I/O without changing the stateid selected.

Terminating the RPC in rpc_call_prepare is not enough on its own.  The
done callback reads the -EIO as a data server connection error, forgets
the device ID, and resets the I/O to pNFS (or, for an NFSv4 data
server, possibly to the MDS).  After a reset to pNFS a new LAYOUTGET is
granted and rpc_call_prepare fails the I/O again, without end.  The
existing NFS_CONTEXT_BAD check does not loop, since the open state is
then invalid and pnfs_update_layout() fails the reset I/O, but it still
forgets the device ID.

So when an RPC that was never sent fails and the open context is bad,
the open state is invalid, or the lock is lost, complete it with -EIO
without error handling.  An RPC that was sent and failed is handled as
before, so a real data server error is still reported to the MDS.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of Service via memory leak in NFSv4 pNFS address list cleanup
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

NFSv4/pnfs: Free the netid when draining a data-server address list

nfs4_pnfs_ds_addr_free() releases all three of an address entry's
allocations, but the four sites that drain a decoded list before it
reaches a data server open-code the loop and free only da_remotestr and
the entry, leaking da_netid.  Both layout drivers drain that list when
nfs4_pnfs_ds_add() returned a data server already in the cache, and
again on their error exits.

Lift the drain into nfs4_pnfs_ds_addr_list_free() so an address list has
one owner.  A striping mount reaches the cached case on nearly every
GETDEVICEINFO, since many deviceIDs name the same data servers.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Information disclosure in SMB client via malformed FIND response parameters
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: reject short or out-of-range FIND response parameters

CIFSFindFirst() and CIFSFindNext() read the SearchHandle, SearchCount,
EndofSearch and LastNameOffset of a TRANS2_FIND_FIRST2 or
TRANS2_FIND_NEXT2 response at ParameterOffset. validate_t2() bounds
the offset at 1024 and ParameterCount below 512, and nothing compares
them with the number of bytes SendReceive() copied into the buffer or
with the size of the response parameters. smb_init() places the
request and the response in the same cifs_request allocation and
cifs_buf_get() clears only the start of it, so a short response with a
ParameterOffset past its end has the search handle, the entry count,
the end-of-search flag and the last-entry offset read out of the
request that was just sent, or out of whatever the allocation held
before, and a ParameterCount smaller than the parameters has them read
past the end of the parameter block. The reads stay inside the
allocation, but what they return is not part of the response, and
CIFSFindFirst() then hands back a search handle the server never sent.
That handle is sent back to the server in the next FIND_NEXT2 or
FIND_CLOSE2, so two bytes of the buffer leak at an offset the server
picks.

SMB1 is not negotiated by default; reaching this code requires an
explicit vers=1.0 mount.

Reject a response whose parameter area is smaller than the response
parameters or extends past the received length, returning smb_EIO2()
with a new smb_eio_traces value for each of the two responses, like
the other response checks this file gained since v6.19. Backports to
trees before v6.19 need smb_EIO2() replaced with -EINVAL and the
trace.h hunk dropped.

A conforming server is not affected. The parameter block of a
transaction response is part of the SMB, so ParameterOffset +
ParameterCount cannot exceed the smbCalcSize() bytes that
SendReceive() copies, and the response parameters are 10 bytes for
FIND_FIRST2 and 8 bytes for FIND_NEXT2, which is what
T2_FFIRST_RSP_PARMS and T2_FNEXT_RSP_PARMS hold.

This patch depends on "smb: client: reject FIND data areas that run
past the received response", whose declarations it extends.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Information disclosure via malformed SMB directory search response
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: reject FIND data areas that run past the received response

CIFSFindFirst() and CIFSFindNext() take the directory entries of a
TRANS2_FIND_FIRST2 or TRANS2_FIND_NEXT2 response from DataOffset for
DataCount bytes. validate_t2() bounds DataOffset at 1024 and
ParameterCount + DataCount by the byte count, and nothing compares
DataOffset + DataCount with the number of bytes SendReceive() copied
into the buffer.

smb_init() places the request and the response in the same
cifs_request allocation and cifs_buf_get() clears only the start of
it, so a short response whose data area extends past its end has
srch_entries_start point at bytes of the request that was just sent,
or at whatever the allocation held before, and those bytes are parsed
as directory entries. cifs_readdir() and find_cifs_entry() walk the
entries with nxt_dir_entry(), which checks every entry but the first
of a response against the end of the SMB; cifs_query_path_info() and
cifs_backup_query_path_info() read the first entry with no check at
all. Those reads stay inside the allocation, but what they return is
not part of the response. The last entry, which LastNameOffset locates
relative to the data area, is bounded against the received response
by an earlier patch of this series, as is every entry that
cifs_fill_dirent() parses; the walk itself and the two query functions
are not.

SMB1 is not negotiated by default; reaching this code requires an
explicit vers=1.0 mount.

Reject a response whose data area extends past the received length,
with the -EINVAL that validate_t2() returns for the other malformed
transaction responses. cifs_query_path_info() and
cifs_backup_query_path_info() still read a whole entry from a data
area that may be smaller than one; that is not changed here.

A conforming server is not affected. The data block of a transaction
response is part of the SMB, so DataOffset + DataCount cannot exceed
the smbCalcSize() bytes that SendReceive() copies; coalesce_t2()
appends each secondary response to the data area and adds its length
to both DataCount and the byte count, which keeps that relation.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: File system metadata corruption via incorrect block accounting in XFS repair
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfs: don't subtract excess usage twice when computing agf_btreeblks

LOLLM noticed that the free space btree repair code calculates
agf_btreeblks from the number of blocks we wrote to rebuild the free
space btrees (minus the roots).  That's correct.  However, it observes
that we subtract the "excess" reservation, which is not correct.  Fix
this accounting problem.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: improper access control via stale cached ACLs during XFS repair
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfs: always forget cached ACLs if the attr fork swap succeeds

LOLLM complains that xrep_xattr_rebuild_tree omits the xfs_forget_acl
call if the attr fork swap succeeds (and hence the acls might have
changed) but reaping the old attr fork fails.  Fix it so that we always
purge the cached acls if the swap succeeds, even if subsequent steps do
not.  This avoids some cache coherency problems with access controls.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of service in OverlayFS via empty security capabilities
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ovl: skip copy up of empty security.capability

ovl_copy_xattr() gives up if it can't read an attribute that
listxattr() has named.  An empty security.capability, which anybody has
been able to store on any file for a long time, is such a case: it is
listed, and getxattr() has nothing to return for it.  A file in a lower
layer that carries one can't be copied up: it can't be written to,
renamed or have its mode changed.

There is nothing to copy if there are no data.  Go on with the next
one.

[amir: treat -EINVAL as no capability too, and do the same in
 ovl_copy_up_meta_inode_data()]

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of Service in OverlayFS via race condition during file creation
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ovl: set the revalidate flags after d_instantiate()

stat() of a file on an overlayfs mount triggers a kernel warning and
fails with ECHILD if another task is creating that file at the same
time. This happens on an overlay with a FUSE upper layer, which is the
layer where overlayfs creates new files. Write access to a directory on
such an overlay is all a user needs to run the two tasks.

The revalidate flags are DCACHE_OP_REVALIDATE and
DCACHE_OP_WEAK_REVALIDATE. They tell path walk to call ->d_revalidate()
or ->d_weak_revalidate() on a dentry, so that the filesystem can check
that the cached dentry is still valid. An overlay dentry only has one of
these flags if a dentry in one of its layers has it. FUSE dentries have
the first one.

When a flag is set on an overlay dentry, path walk calls
ovl_dentry_revalidate_common(). That function only expects a dentry
without an inode in RCU walk, while the dentry is being destroyed. For
such a dentry outside of RCU walk, it hits a WARN_ON() and
returns -ECHILD. So a negative overlay dentry must never have the flags
set.

ovl_instantiate() breaks this rule. When a task creates a file, the
overlay dentry for the new name is hashed but still negative.
ovl_instantiate() then works in this order:

- It copies the flags from the new upper dentry to the overlay dentry.
- It calls ovl_get_inode(), which can sleep in a getxattr request to the
  FUSE server.
- Only then does it call d_instantiate().

A second task that looks up the name between the first step and the last
finds a negative dentry with the flags set and revalidates it.

Reproduced with a FUSE server that delays its getxattr reply: stat() of
a name that was being created hit the WARN_ON() and failed with ECHILD.

Fix this by setting the flags after d_instantiate().

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: information disclosure via uninitialized extended attribute copy-up in OverlayFS
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ovl: do not copy up an xattr value that was never read

Copy-up stores uninitialized kernel memory in an xattr of the upper
file, where the user can read it.

ovl_copy_xattr() may only pass bytes to ovl_do_setxattr() that
ovl_do_getxattr() has read. When the read fails with -ERANGE the
function asks for the size again, and if the new size fits the buffer
it stores the buffer although nothing was read into it. The buffer
comes from kvmalloc(), or it still holds the value of the previous
xattr.

A FUSE lower layer that answers every sized GETXATTR with -ERANGE made
copy-up store 4096 bytes that the server never sent, with a kernel
pointer in them, as an xattr of the upper file.

Fix this by failing the copy-up with -EIO when the size that follows
-ERANGE fits the buffer.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Information disclosure via uninitialized memory in s390 vmcp driver
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

s390/vmcp: Initialize full session info to zero

The cma_alloc bit as well as the response can contain old data.
cma_release will not free the kmalloced memory in that case and
the response code might leak kernel stack data to CAP_SYS_ADMIN
users.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: File system corruption in F2FS via roll-forward recovery
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

f2fs: release a removed xattr node in roll-forward recovery

When xattrs shrink enough to fit in the inline xattr area,
write_all_xattrs() truncates the xattr node and clears i_xattr_nid. If
the file is then fsynced without a checkpoint, only the inode block is
written, with i_xattr_nid of 0.

Roll-forward recovery starts from the checkpointed inode, whose
i_xattr_nid still points to the old xattr node.
f2fs_recover_inline_xattr() copies only the inline xattr area, and
f2fs_update_inode() writes the old i_xattr_nid back. So the inode keeps
the stale xattr node:

 - The node block is never released, and fsck reports "nonzero bytes in
   xattr space after end of list".
 - If the inline xattr list ends exactly at the end of the inline area,
   its terminator is read from the stale node, and the removed xattrs
   come back after recovery.

When the fsynced inode has no xattr node but the checkpointed one has,
release the old xattr node as truncate_node() does: check its block
address, invalidate the block and drop its node cache, which may still
be dirty.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of Service via excessive block traversal in f2fs
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

f2fs: return -EIO for a lost inode block after cp_error

After cp_error, dirty node caches are dropped without being written.
If such an inode was never written, its NAT entry is still NEW_ADDR,
and reading its inode block returns -ENOENT.

f2fs_get_dnode_of_data() passes that -ENOENT up, and callers take it
as a hole. Since the inode block is missing, the next offset can only
advance one block, so fiemap walks block by block up to maxbytes,
about 2^30 blocks, while holding the inode lock. It took hours in a
power-off recovery test after shutdown and blocked unlink and umount
on the file.

Return -EIO instead of -ENOENT when the inode block itself is missing
after cp_error or shutdown. A missing direct or indirect node is still
reported as -ENOENT.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: execution restriction bypass via POSIX ACL on sealed memfd
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/shmem: honour F_SEAL_EXEC when an ACL is set

The owner of a memfd sealed with F_SEAL_EXEC can still change its
execute bits by setting a POSIX access ACL. With CONFIG_TMPFS_POSIX_ACL,
this lets an unprivileged owner make a non-executable memfd executable,
bypassing vm.memfd_noexec=2.

simple_set_acl() updates i_mode directly, bypassing the seal check in
shmem_setattr(). Add shmem_set_acl() to check the resulting mode. Share
the F_SEAL_EXEC check with shmem_setattr() using memfd_check_seals_mode()
in include/linux/memfd.h.

Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private.

[ david: use common helper; simplify description ]

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of Service via memory leak in ARM64 kexec_file retry loop
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

arm64: kexec_file: Fix elf_headers memory leak in retry loop

A retry allocates new elf headers and overwrites image->elf_headers,
leaking the previous buffer.

Free it before assigning.

[catalin.marinas@arm.com: drop the redundant NULL check before vfree()]

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Data corruption in UDF file system via improper extent handling
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

udf: don't use eloc after the end of the unallocated space table

When udf_next_aext() returns 0, its eloc, elen and etype outputs hold
no defined value.  Two walks of the unallocated space table still use
eloc after the walk has reached the end of the table.

udf_table_prealloc_blocks() looks for a free extent starting at
first_block and decides whether it found one by comparing eloc with
first_block after the walk.  If the table's list ends in a continuation
descriptor that leads to an empty allocation extent, eloc is then the
block of that allocation extent, which is in use, and if that is
first_block, the block is handed out as preallocation.  Once
udf_discard_prealloc() no longer frees the wrong block, this is what
still makes fsx in generic/091 and generic/263 read back bad data on a
table, in about one run in four.  Only take the extent if the walk
stopped at it.

When udf_table_free_blocks() cannot merge the freed blocks into an
existing extent, it appends a new one and sets only its block number,
so the partition reference comes from whatever eloc held after the
walk, and with long allocation descriptors it is written to disk.  For
a table without extents, eloc was never set.  Take the partition
reference from the freed blocks instead.  Short allocation descriptors
do not store the partition reference, which is why this half remains a
latent long-descriptor fix rather than a reproduced failure.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: ext2: Failure to persist file size metadata during direct synchronous writes
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ext2: preserve IOMAP_F_DIRTY for extending direct writes

ext2_iomap_begin() sets IOMAP_F_DIRTY for writes that may extend i_size,
but clears the flag after ext2_get_blocks(). When the write uses an
existing mapped block, iomap can then use FUA and skip
generic_write_sync(), even though ext2_dio_write_end_io() updates the
inode size. An O_DSYNC write can therefore return without persisting
the new size.

For example, on a FUA-capable device, a 512-byte O_DIRECT|O_DSYNC write
at offset 512 into a fsynced one-byte file returns successfully and
extends the in-memory size to 1024, while an immediate read of the
on-disk inode still shows size 1. An explicit fsync persists the new
size.

Move setting of IOMAP_F_DIRTY after the initialization.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of Service via caiaq input setup memory leak
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ALSA: caiaq: free the EP4 URB when input setup fails

The three controllers that use the EP4 input URB allocate it before
checking the endpoint type and before registering the input device. On
failure they jump to exit_free_idev, which clears cdev->input_dev but
leaves cdev->ep4_in_urb set. The card teardown then calls
snd_usb_caiaq_input_free(), which returns early because input_dev is
NULL, so the URB is never freed.

Release the URB before dropping the input device on the error path.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of Service via cross-tunnel session manipulation in L2TP
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

l2tp: only return sessions of the given tunnel in l2tp_session_get()

Commit 5f77c18ea556 ("l2tp: use IDR for all session lookups") made
pppol2tp_connect() and the netlink session commands find sessions with
l2tp_session_get(), passing the socket of the tunnel they name.

L2TPv3 session IDs are unique per network namespace, except that
sessions carried over UDP are only unique per UDP socket, the socket of
their tunnel. However, l2tp_v3_session_get() only checks the socket when
another session has the same session ID. Otherwise it returns the
session, whichever tunnel it belongs to. As of now, a session command
that names the wrong tunnel acts on a session of another tunnel, and a
PPPoL2TP socket for a second L2TPv3 tunnel fails with EEXIST, because it
finds session 0 of the first tunnel.

The issue can be reproduced with:

    ip l2tp add tunnel tunnel_id 3 peer_tunnel_id 3 encap udp \
        local 127.0.0.1 remote 127.0.0.1 udp_sport 5003 udp_dport 6003
    ip l2tp add tunnel tunnel_id 4 peer_tunnel_id 4 encap udp \
        local 127.0.0.1 remote 127.0.0.1 udp_sport 5004 udp_dport 6004
    ip l2tp add session tunnel_id 3 session_id 7 peer_session_id 7
    ip l2tp del session tunnel_id 4 session_id 7
    ip l2tp show session

Before that commit, the delete fails with "No such device", and session
7 of tunnel 3 is still listed. After that commit, the delete succeeds,
and session 7 of tunnel 3 is gone.

This patch will make l2tp_session_get() return NULL when the L2TPv3
session it finds does not belong to the given socket. The receive path
calls l2tp_v3_session_get() directly and is not changed.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of Service via memory leak in amdgpu buffer import error handling
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/amdgpu: drop the dma-buf reference when a KFD import fails

import_obj_create() takes a reference on the dma-buf for the new kgd_mem,
but the error path after validating the BO doesn't drop it. Since the
validation reserves the BO interruptibly, an import failing with
-ERESTARTSYS leaks the exported BO with its memory, and keeps the module
in use.

Importing a 64 MiB VRAM BO in a loop while getting SIGUSR1
every 20 us and another thread changes the BO's mappings:

  INFO: 171821 imports, VRAM used before 65 MiB, after 129 MiB
  modprobe: FATAL: Module amdgpu is in use.

Drop the reference, and free the sync object and the mutex of the kgd_mem
as well. With that VRAM usage returns to 65 MiB after the same test.

(cherry picked from commit b4d1eca2729840148ff2ea957724ce764ca5a94e)

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of service via improper DDC pin cleanup in AMD display driver
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/amd/display: Avoid closing unowned DDC pins

[WHY]
dal_ddc_open() cleans up pins it acquires on later failures. If the
data-pin open fails, this attempt acquired nothing. If opening the
clock pin or configuring fails, dal_ddc_open() closes the pins it
opened. An extra dal_ddc_close() is unnecessary and unsafe:
GPIO_RESULT_ALREADY_OPENED can mean AUX owns the existing handles,
and closing them here would disrupt AUX.

[HOW]
Remove the extra dal_ddc_close() from the failed-open path.

(cherry picked from commit 175ae7772b68757b4932f34ff862923cab7abe21)

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of Service via memory leak in XFS btree operations
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfs: fix temporary cursor leak in btree shift corruption paths

In xfs_btree_lshift and xfs_btree_rshift, when XFS_IS_CORRUPT detects
an invalid firstrec/lastrec result after xfs_btree_dup_cursor has
successfully allocated a temporary cursor, the error path jumps to
error0 which returns without freeing tcur.  This leaks the cursor
memory, the xfs_group reference, and the per-level buffer references
held by the duplicated cursor.  Jump to error1 instead, which calls
xfs_btree_del_cursor(tcur, XFS_BTREE_ERROR) to properly release all
resources.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of Service via 32-bit integer overflow in page writeback
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/page-writeback: avoid 32-bit overflow in dirty threshold shares

The ratios used by __wb_calc_thresh() are scaled to parts per million, but
the threshold and ratio operands are unsigned long.  On 32-bit kernels,
their multiplication can wrap before the result is assigned to u64.

For example, with a threshold of 25600 pages and the default maximum ratio
of 1000000, wb_max_thresh becomes 4125 pages instead of 25600.  The shared
threshold and minimum share calculations can overflow in the same way,
producing incorrect per-writeback dirty limits.

Use a u64 threshold for the three ratio multiplications and div_u64() to
retain the existing division order and rounding.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of Service via redundant MSR processing on failed nested VM-entry
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: nVMX: Process each host MSR entry at most once when unwinding failed VM-Entry

Add a missing "break" in the inner for-loop of the open coded mess that
unwinds MSRs back to the pre-VM-Enter state when VMLAUNCH/VMRESUME VM-Fails
due to a consistency check that is caught by hardware but missed by KVM.
I.e. move on to the next MSR in the VM-Entry load list after performing a
write using a value found in the VM-Exit load list.  Processing *every*
matching entry in the VM-Exit load list makes the processing quadratic,
which is problematic if the load lists are full of MSRs that are expensive
to emulate.  E.g. writing APIC_BASE triggers kvm_recalculate_apic_map() and
a whole pile of unnecessary work.

Functionally, arbitrarily restoring the value of the first matching entry
is "fine", because none of this is architecturally correct: the load lists
are never supposed to have been used in the first place.  In practice, it's
likely a moot point as no well-behaved VMM will have multiple, diverging
entries in the load lists.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of Service via memory leak in vhost-vdpa
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

vhost-vdpa: fix pinned page leak in vhost_vdpa_pa_map() error path

When pin_user_pages() or vhost_vdpa_map() fails, vhost_vdpa_pa_map()
is supposed to unpin the pages pinned after the last successfully
mapped chunk, i.e. the range [map_pfn, last_pfn]. The unpin is guarded
by nchunks, but nchunks is reset to 0 every time a chunk is mapped from
inside the current page list, so a failure after any such boundary
leaves that pending range pinned forever. With physically scattered
memory nearly every page list contains a boundary, so the leak happens
on practically every failed IOTLB update.

The pending range is non-empty exactly when a page has been pinned,
which last_pfn already tells us, so drop nchunks and test last_pfn.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Quota limit bypass via discarded tmpfs soft limits
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

tmpfs: keep the quota soft limits of an unused id

When the last reference to a dquot goes away, shmem_release_dquot()
stores its limits in the rb tree of the mount, unless
shmem_is_empty_dquot() says that there is nothing worth storing. That
function looks at the usage and at the two hard limits only.

So if the administrator sets nothing but soft limits for an id that owns
no file yet, the entry is thrown away as soon as the dquot that
Q_SETQUOTA used is released, and the id never gets to see a limit.

To fix it, compare the soft limits as well: an entry can be empty only if
both soft limits are zero as well, which is exactly what
shmem_acquire_dquot() sets for a new entry.

Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Josef Bacik in private.

[ david: slightly adjusted description ]

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of service via race condition in batman-adv translation table updates
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

batman-adv: tt: don't drop local events queued during TVLV update

batadv_tt_tvlv_container_update() read the number of local changes without
holding changes_list_lock. batadv_tt_local_event() is not serialized by
the commit_lock and can queue new events before the changes_list is
flushed:

  CPU0                          CPU1
  batadv_tt_tvlv_container_update()
    num = ...local_changes;
                                batadv_tt_local_event()
                                  list_add_tail(...);
                                  ...local_changes++;
    spin_lock_bh(&...changes_list_lock);
    /* only num events copied but all freed */

The additional events were freed without ever being sent. Other nodes will
only notice this via a CRC mismatch and must request the full table.

The number of changes and the changes_list must therefore be taken
atomically. Events queued afterwards then stay in the tt.changes_list for
the next TT round.

The changes can no longer be kept for the next round when the TVLV buffer
allocation fails. But they would be sent with a skipped TTVN anyway, so the
other nodes have to request the full table in this case either way. The
last changeset is only dropped in this case when the TTVN was incremented.
Without new changes, it still describes the current TTVN.

Previously, the unconsumed changes caused a retry of the TVLV container
update in the next commit round. Since the changes are now consumed, the
next round would only take the path without changes and wait for
BATADV_TT_OGM_APPEND_MAX rounds before updating the container again. Until
then, the outdated container with the previous TTVN would still be
announced. The ogm_append_cnt is therefore reset on failure to retry the
update in the next OGM interval.

This doesn't make the CRC consistent with the announced changeset. The
local table modifications are still not serialized with the commit and
batadv_tt_local_transition_new() can still make a client part of the CRC
for which the event is only part of the next TT round. Such an
inconsistency is detected by the CRC check of the other nodes and solved
via a full table request.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of Service via memory leak in 9P USB gadget driver
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net/9p/usbg: fix out_req buffer leak in disable_usb9pfs

usb9pfs->out_req is allocated with alloc_ep_req(), which also
allocates the request's data buffer (req->buf). disable_usb9pfs()
frees it with plain usb_ep_free_request(), which only frees the
usb_request structure itself and leaks req->buf on every close.

Use free_ep_req() instead, matching the allocator, as documented by
its own comment ("Requests allocated via alloc_ep_req() *must* be
freed by free_ep_req()").

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of Service via memory leak in 9P USB gadget transport
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net/9p/usbg: call disable_usb9pfs() from usb9pfs_disable()

usb9pfs_disable() is the usb_function ->disable callback, invoked by
the composite gadget core whenever the host resets or unconfigures
the gadget. The gadget function API requires this callback to disable
its endpoints; every other in-tree function driver does so from its
->disable hook.

usb9pfs_disable() never called disable_usb9pfs(), so the IN/OUT
endpoints and their usb_request objects were left active and
allocated across a host-driven disable. When the host later
reconfigures the device, enable_usb9pfs() calls alloc_requests() again
and unconditionally overwrites usb9pfs->in_req/out_req, permanently
leaking the previous allocations, while the endpoints themselves are
left enabled underneath the function's own idea of being disabled.

Call disable_usb9pfs() before reinit_completion(&usb9pfs->send),
mirroring the same sequence already used in p9_usbg_close(). Placing
it before the reinit_completion() also ensures usb_ep_disable() has
synchronously flushed any requests still queued in hardware before the
completion is reset, closing the same race that motivated resetting
the completion here in the first place.

Vulnerabilities.Title: [Kernel: Unprivileged user can freeze journald]
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:  x ...
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfs: always report inode repair setup failures

LOLLM noticed that xchk_setup_inode silently discards errors being
returned by xrep_setup_inode.  Fix that, and fix the stub macro so that
it actually "returns" a value.

Vulnerabilities.Title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:  x ...
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfs: check fork type against dabtree block magic number

LOLLM complains that we fail to flag dabtree blocks that should never be
associated with the file fork -- data forks can't point to xattr leaves,
and attr forks can't point to dirent blocks.  Add the missing checks.

Vulnerabilities.Title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:  x ...
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfs: don't proceed with xattr repair if the live update fails

LOLLM observes that we ought to make one last check for failed live
updates before replacing the xattr structure.  Let's be cautious here.

Vulnerabilities.Title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:  s ...
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

s390/probes: Fix wrong opcode for cgrb fixup

The last byte of the cgrb instruction is 0xe4, however the probes code
compares against 0xe6. Fix it.

Vulnerabilities.Title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:  n ...
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net/9p/usbg: also disable endpoints on p9_usbg_close

The close function has to fully reverse the state change of 9p_create
(mount) and the potential call of set_alt(1). This includes to ensure
that the usage of the endpoints is not active any more.

Vulnerabilities.Title: util-linux: util-linux: failed external mount helper still runs privileged X-mount post-hooks
Vulnerabilities.Description: util-linux versions through 2.41.5 and 2.42.2 fail to check mount helper exit status before running post-mount hooks, allowing unprivileged users to execute privileged operations on pre-existing filesystems. Attackers can exploit X-mount.idmap or X-mount.owner hooks to clone filesystems with inherited suid bits or modify target inode permissions after a helper fails, achieving privilege escalation.

Vulnerabilities.Title: util-linux: util-linux: nsenter --join-cgroup leaks root cgroup migration authority
Vulnerabilities.Description: The nsenter --join-cgroup option opens the target cgroup.procs file as root and leaves that file descriptor open across later namespace and credential changes and across execve(). Because the kernel checks later cgroup migrations using the credentials from the original open, a program run in an attacker-controlled target can inherit root's ability to move host processes between cgroups. After a privileged operator uses --join-cgroup against that target, an unprivileged user can migrate and terminate unrelated root processes.

Vulnerabilities.Title: util-linux: util-linux: X-mount.subdir detached-tree resolution can escape via intermediate symlinks
Vulnerabilities.Description: The X-mount.subdir option uses a detached-tree fast path on Linux 6.15 and later and passes the configured subdirectory to open_tree() with AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW. That flag does not stop intermediate symlink traversal or keep resolution inside the newly mounted filesystem. A local unprivileged user with an fstab-authorized X-mount.subdir entry can attach a host path at the intended mountpoint.

Vulnerabilities.Title: util-linux: util-linux: restricted bind mounts do not pin the source, allowing X-mount.owner/group/mode redirection
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in util-linux. Restricted bind mounts take the source path from fstab but do not pin that source before the privileged mount. A local unprivileged user who can replace the authorized source or a writable ancestor can redirect SUID mount(8) to bind another host directory. If the fstab entry also sets X-mount.owner, X-mount.group, or X-mount.mode, root then changes ownership or mode on that redirected inode.

Vulnerabilities.Title: util-linux: util-linux: Access control bypass due to improper hostname canonicalization
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in util-linux. Improper hostname canonicalization in the `login(1)` utility, when invoked with the `-h` option, can modify the supplied remote hostname before setting `PAM_RHOST`. A remote attacker could exploit this by providing a specially crafted hostname, potentially bypassing host-based Pluggable Authentication Modules (PAM) access control rules that rely on fully qualified domain names. This could lead to unauthorized access.

Vulnerabilities.Title: util-linux: partial disclosure of arbitrary files in chfn and chsh when compiled with libreadline
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in the util-linux chfn and chsh utilities when compiled with Readline support. The Readline library uses an "INPUTRC" environment variable to get a path to the library config file. When the library cannot parse the specified file, it prints an error message containing data from the file. This flaw allows an unprivileged user to read root-owned files, potentially leading to privilege escalation. This flaw affects util-linux versions prior to 2.37.4.

Vulnerabilities.Title: initscripts in rPath Linux 1 sets insecure permissions for the /var/lo ...
Vulnerabilities.Description: initscripts in rPath Linux 1 sets insecure permissions for the /var/log/btmp file, which allows local users to obtain sensitive information regarding authentication attempts.  NOTE: because sshd detects the insecure permissions and does not log certain events, this also prevents sshd from logging failed authentication attempts by remote attackers.

Vulnerabilities.Title: shadow-utils: Default subordinate ID configuration in /etc/login.defs could lead to compromise
Vulnerabilities.Description: shadow-utils (aka shadow) 4.4 through 4.17.0 establishes a default /etc/subuid behavior (e.g., uid 100000 through 165535 for the first user account) that can realistically conflict with the uids of users defined on locally administered networks, potentially leading to account takeover, e.g., by leveraging newuidmap for access to an NFS home directory (or same-host resources in the case of remote logins by these local network users). NOTE: it may also be argued that system administrators should not have assigned uids, within local networks, that are within the range that can occur in /etc/subuid.

Vulnerabilities.Title: [more related to CVE-2005-4890]
m4: unquoted output of maketemp and mkstemp
Vulnerabilities.Description: The (1) maketemp and (2) mkstemp builtin functions in GNU m4 before 1.4.11 do not quote their output when a file is created, which might allow context-dependent attackers to trigger a macro expansion, leading to unspecified use of an incorrect filename.

Vulnerabilities.Title: m4: code execution via -F argument
Vulnerabilities.Description: Unspecified vulnerability in GNU m4 before 1.4.11 might allow context-dependent attackers to execute arbitrary code, related to improper handling of filenames specified with the -F option.  NOTE: it is not clear when this issue crosses privilege boundaries.

Vulnerabilities.Title: mariadb: MariaDB server: SQL injection vulnerability via improper handling of big5 character set with mysql_real_escape_string()
Vulnerabilities.Description: MariaDB server is a community developed fork of MySQL server. In versions 3.3.18 and 3.4.8, an application that was taking non-validated user input, escaping it with mysql_real_escape_string() and sending it to the database using text protocol and big5 character set was vulnerable to SQL injections, even though mysql_real_escape_string() was supposed to prevent them. This issue has been patched in versions 3.3.19 and 3.4.9.

Vulnerabilities.Title: mariadb: MariaDB Server: Arbitrary code execution via wsrep_notify_cmd
Vulnerabilities.Description: MariaDB server is a community developed fork of MySQL server. Versions 10.6.1 through 10.6.26, 10.11.1 through 10.11.17, 11.4.1 through 11.4.11, 11.8.1 through 11.8.7, and 12.3.1 with  `wsrep_notify_cmd` enabled would execute shell commands embedded in the name of the joiner node. This is fixed in 10.6.27, 10.11.18, 11.4.12, 11.8.8, and 12.3.2. As a workaround, anyone who cannot upgrade now should disable `wsrep_notify_cmd`.

Vulnerabilities.Title: mariadb: MariaDB: Unauthorized table access via unencoded partition names
Vulnerabilities.Description: MariaDB server is a community developed fork of MySQL server. From 10.11.1 until 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 11.8.9, 12.3.3, and 13.0.2, ALTER TABLE ... CONVERT ... PARTITION does not apply filename encoding to user-specified partition names before using them in filesystem path construction. An authenticated database user can use a partition name requiring filename escaping to make the conversion operate on table files the user is not authorized to access, allowing unauthorized table reads or modifications. This issue is fixed in versions 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 11.8.9, 12.3.3, and 13.0.2.

Vulnerabilities.Title: mariadb: mariadb: Arbitrary code execution via CONNECT engine out-of-bounds write
Vulnerabilities.Description: MariaDB server is a community developed fork of MySQL server. From 10.6.1 until 10.6.28, 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 11.8.9, 12.3.3, and 13.0.2, the CONNECT engine's DOS table type used an incorrect boundary check that permitted a one-byte null write beyond a stack buffer at an attacker-controlled offset. An authenticated user able to use the CONNECT engine could cause a crash and potentially remote code execution. This issue is fixed in versions 10.6.28, 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 11.8.9, 12.3.3, and 13.0.2.

Vulnerabilities.Title: mariadb: mariadb: Privilege escalation via environment variable injection during service restart
Vulnerabilities.Description: MariaDB server is a community developed fork of MySQL server. From 10.6.1 until 10.6.28, 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 11.8.9, 12.3.3, and 13.0.2, the mariadb.service unit used /run/mysqld/wsrep-new-cluster during the next service restart. A database user with FILE privilege and a secure-file-priv configuration permitting writes to /run/mysqld could create that file and inject attacker-controlled environment values into the restarted service. This issue is fixed in versions 10.6.28, 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 11.8.9, 12.3.3, and 13.0.2.

Vulnerabilities.Title: mariadb: mariadb: Privilege escalation via unescaped newlines in view parser
Vulnerabilities.Description: MariaDB server is a community developed fork of MySQL server. From 10.6.1 until 10.6.28, 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 11.8.9, 12.3.3, and 13.0.2, the MariaDB view FRM parser did not safely encode embedded newline characters in a username. An account with CREATE USER and CREATE VIEW WITH GRANT OPTION could create a crafted username containing additional view metadata, causing the parser to interpret part of the username as security metadata and potentially escalating database privileges. This issue is fixed in versions 10.6.28, 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 11.8.9, 12.3.3, and 13.0.2.

Vulnerabilities.Title: mariadb: Arbitrary Code Execution via improper parameter validation during State Snapshot Transfer
Vulnerabilities.Description: MariaDB server is a community developed fork of MySQL server. From versions 10.6.1 to before 10.6.26, 10.11.1 to before 10.11.17, 11.4.1 to before 11.4.11, 11.8.1 to before 11.8.7, and 12.3.1, during the SST the donor node is interpolating parameters that the joiner sent into the command line. Not all parameters were properly validated which could allow a malicious joiner to execute arbitrary shell commands on the donor side via the mariabackup SST method. This issue has been patched in versions 10.6.26, 10.11.17, 11.4.11, 11.8.7, and 12.3.2.

Vulnerabilities.Title: mariadb: mbstream: Unauthorized file creation via path traversal
Vulnerabilities.Description: MariaDB server is a community developed fork of MySQL server. From versions 10.6.1 to before 10.6.26, 10.11.1 to before 10.11.17, 11.4.1 to before 11.4.11, 11.8.1 to before 11.8.7, and 12.3.1, mbstream did not check for /../ in the path when unpacking the archive. A proper backup can never contain such paths, but a specially crafted archive could have caused mbstream to create files outside of the target-dir path. This issue has been patched in versions 10.6.26, 10.11.17, 11.4.11, 11.8.7, and 12.3.2.

Vulnerabilities.Title: mariadb: Arbitrary code execution via improper parameter validation during SST
Vulnerabilities.Description: MariaDB server is a community developed fork of MySQL server. From versions 10.6.1 to before 10.6.27, 10.11.1 to before 10.11.18, 11.4.1 to before 11.4.12, 11.8.1 to before 11.8.8, and 12.3.1, during the SST the donor node is interpolating parameters that the joiner sent into the command line. Not all parameters were properly validated which could allow a malicious joiner to execute arbitrary shell commands on the donor side via the rsync SST method. This issue has been patched in versions 10.6.27, 10.11.18, 11.4.12, 11.8.8, and 12.3.2.

Vulnerabilities.Title: mariadb: Arbitrary code execution via global system variable manipulation by a high-privileged user
Vulnerabilities.Description: MariaDB server is a community developed fork of MySQL server. From versions 10.6.1 to before 10.6.27, 10.11.1 to before 10.11.18, 11.4.1 to before 11.4.12, 11.8.1 to before 11.8.8, and 12.3.1, a high-privileged MariaDB user could've used wsrep_sst_receive_address or wsrep_sst_donor global system variables to execute shell commands as the uid of the mariadbd process on the galera joiner node. This issue has been patched in versions 10.6.27, 10.11.18, 11.4.12, 11.8.8, and 12.3.2.

Vulnerabilities.Title: mariadb: MariaDB: Out-of-bound buffer write on in `ST_AsText` of nested GeometryCollections
Vulnerabilities.Description: MariaDB server is a community developed fork of MySQL server. From 10.6.1 until 10.6.28, 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 11.8.9, 12.3.3, and 13.0.2, ST_AsText can write beyond an allocated output buffer when converting deeply nested GeometryCollections because recursive WKT serialization does not account for bytes consumed or reserve sufficient space. A low-privileged remote attacker can submit a specially crafted GIS object to corrupt memory and potentially achieve code execution when combined with another vulnerability. This issue is fixed in versions 10.6.28, 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 11.8.9, 12.3.3, and 13.0.2.

Vulnerabilities.Title: mariadb: mariadb: SQL injection via improper identifier quoting
Vulnerabilities.Description: MariaDB server is a community developed fork of MySQL server. From 10.6.1 until 10.6.28, 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 11.8.9, 12.3.3, and 13.0.2, SHOW CREATE SERVER, SHOW CREATE USER, and mariadb-dump are affected because each does not consistently quote identifiers and values when serializing SQL. A low-privileged attacker can trigger the issue when an attacker-created object with crafted identifiers or values is included in SHOW output or a dump, then create an object with crafted identifiers or values so generated SQL contains injected statements and execute attacker-injected SQL when the poisoned output is applied. This issue is fixed in versions 10.6.28, 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 11.8.9, 12.3.3, and 13.0.2.

Vulnerabilities.Title: mariadb: MariaDB: Numerous issues caused by historical #mysql50# tablename encoding bypass.
Vulnerabilities.Description: MariaDB server is a community developed fork of MySQL server. From 10.6.1 until 10.6.28, 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 11.8.9, 12.3.3, and 13.0.2, the #mysql50# bypass prefix is affected because it allows the #mysql50# prefix to bypass normal table-name filesystem encoding. An attacker can trigger the issue with a table name using the #mysql50# prefix, then use a #mysql50# table name to access files under their legacy unencoded name and cause crashes, data corruption, data exfiltration, or remote code execution. This issue is fixed in versions 10.6.28, 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 11.8.9, 12.3.3, and 13.0.2.

Vulnerabilities.Title: mariadb: mariadb: Privilege escalation via empty password in GRANT PROXY statement
Vulnerabilities.Description: MariaDB server is a community developed fork of MySQL server. From 10.6.1 until 10.6.28, 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 11.8.9, 12.3.3, and 13.0.2, the GRANT PROXY statement treats an IDENTIFIED clause with an empty password as though authentication were not specified, causing it to check the wrong grantor privileges. A low-privileged attacker who can name another account can exploit this authorization error to set that account's password. This issue is fixed in versions 10.6.28, 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 11.8.9, 12.3.3, and 13.0.2.

Vulnerabilities.Title: mariadb: mariadb: Information disclosure via embedded null bytes in query cache plugin
Vulnerabilities.Description: MariaDB server is a community developed fork of MySQL server. From 10.6.1 until 10.6.28, 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 11.8.9, 12.3.3, and 13.0.2, the qc_info plugin could be confused by a query containing embedded null bytes. Reading information_schema.query_cache_info after such a query was cached could access data beyond the end of a heap-allocated buffer, potentially disclosing adjacent memory or crashing the server. This issue is fixed in versions 10.6.28, 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 11.8.9, 12.3.3, and 13.0.2.

Vulnerabilities.Title: mariadb: mariadb: Denial of Service via invalid binary JSON in mysql_json plugin
Vulnerabilities.Description: MariaDB server is a community developed fork of MySQL server. From 10.6.1 until 10.6.28, 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 11.8.9, 12.3.3, and 13.0.2, the mysql_json plugin assumed that imported MySQL tables contained valid MySQL binary JSON data. A specially prepared MySQL table containing invalid JSON data could cause out-of-bounds reads, information disclosure, or a server crash. This issue is fixed in versions 10.6.28, 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 11.8.9, 12.3.3, and 13.0.2.

Vulnerabilities.Title: mariadb: mariadb: Arbitrary code execution via crafted FRM metadata
Vulnerabilities.Description: MariaDB server is a community developed fork of MySQL server. From 10.6.1 until 10.6.28, 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 11.8.9, 12.3.3, and 13.0.2, MariaDB insufficiently validated counts, offsets, lengths, and field boundaries in FRM metadata while opening binary FRM files. An attacker able to place a crafted FRM file in the data directory could trigger out-of-bounds reads or writes, crash the server, or potentially execute code. This issue is fixed in versions 10.6.28, 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 11.8.9, 12.3.3, and 13.0.2.

Vulnerabilities.Title: mariadb: MariaDB: Privilege escalation via ACL cache key collision
Vulnerabilities.Description: MariaDB server is a community developed fork of MySQL server. From 10.6.1 until 10.6.28, 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 11.8.9, 12.3.3, and 13.0.2, MariaDB's ACL cache could generate the same database-privilege cache key for role and localhost user names that matched because both used an empty IP component. An attacker with CREATE USER could create the colliding principal and, when the original principal's database privileges were cached, exercise privileges assigned to the other account. This issue is fixed in versions 10.6.28, 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 11.8.9, 12.3.3, and 13.0.2.

Vulnerabilities.Title: mariadb: MariaDB server: Information disclosure of stored routine definitions due to insufficient privilege check
Vulnerabilities.Description: MariaDB server is a community developed fork of MySQL server. From versions 11.4.1 to before 11.4.11, 11.8.1 to before 11.8.7, and 12.3.1, a user getting EXECUTE access to a stored routine via a role, could see the routine definition even without SHOW CREATE ROUTINE privilege. This issue has been patched in versions 11.4.11, 11.8.7, and 12.3.2.

Vulnerabilities.Title: mariadb: MariaDB: Privilege bypass allows unauthorized file write via subqueries
Vulnerabilities.Description: MariaDB server is a community developed fork of MySQL server. From versions 10.6.1 to before 10.6.26, 10.11.1 to before 10.11.17, 11.4.1 to before 11.4.11, 11.8.1 to before 11.8.7, and 12.3.1, MariaDB allowed SELECT ... INTO OUTFILE and SELECT ... INTO DUMPFILE without verifying the FILE privilege if the FROM clause contained only subqueries. This issue has been patched in versions 10.6.26, 10.11.17, 11.4.11, 11.8.7, and 12.3.2.

Vulnerabilities.Title: mysql: mariadb: Replication unspecified vulnerability (CPU Jul 2026)
Vulnerabilities.Description: Vulnerability in the MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster product of Oracle MySQL (component: Server: Replication).  Supported versions that are affected are MySQL Server: 8.4.0-8.4.10, 9.7.0-9.7.1; MySQL Cluster: 8.0.0-8.0.47, 8.4.0-8.4.10 and  9.7.0-9.7.1. Easily exploitable vulnerability allows high privileged attacker with network access via multiple protocols to compromise MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster.  Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in unauthorized ability to cause a hang or frequently repeatable crash (complete DOS) of MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 4.9 (Availability impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H).

Vulnerabilities.Title: mysql: mariadb: Replication unspecified vulnerability (CPU Jul 2026)
Vulnerabilities.Description: Vulnerability in the MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster product of Oracle MySQL (component: Server: Replication).  Supported versions that are affected are MySQL Server: 8.4.0-8.4.10, 9.7.0-9.7.1; MySQL Cluster: 8.0.0-8.0.47, 8.4.0-8.4.10 and  9.7.0-9.7.1. Difficult to exploit vulnerability allows high privileged attacker with network access via multiple protocols to compromise MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster.  Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in unauthorized ability to cause a hang or frequently repeatable crash (complete DOS) of MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 4.4 (Availability impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H).

Vulnerabilities.Title: mysql: mariadb: Replication unspecified vulnerability (CPU Jul 2026)
Vulnerabilities.Description: Vulnerability in the MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster product of Oracle MySQL (component: Server: Replication).  Supported versions that are affected are MySQL Server: 8.4.0-8.4.10, 9.7.0-9.7.1; MySQL Cluster: 8.0.0-8.0.47, 8.4.0-8.4.10 and  9.7.0-9.7.1. Difficult to exploit vulnerability allows high privileged attacker with logon to the infrastructure where MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster executes to compromise MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster.  Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in takeover of MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 6.4 (Confidentiality, Integrity and Availability impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H).
